replies.author: Coldfriction
replies.body:
I still hate "the cloud" just as I still hate Steam for what it did to gamers when it launched.  I hate AI "slop" sure, but AI is just a tool and like "the cloud" I don't have to use it.

The difference here is that everyone wants OTHERS to not use "the cloud" I mean AI.  I've never had a problem with others doing as they wish and prefer freedom to mob rule.  Having a problem with what others do with their freedom isn't acceptable to me.  Go use "the cloud" or AI and I don't care.  If your product forces me into things I don't like, I won't use it.  IF you use tools I don't like, I won't ever know.  If a company uses Microsoft Azure, and I hate Microsoft, or they internally use Teams or Sharepoint and I hate Microsoft, do I run around screaming about it or do I simply not know what the means and methods are?

Anti-AI is a baseless political-like movement.  It's not going away and the means and methods of product development are essentially never disclosed.

And yes, anti-AI is a prejudice at this point.  I'm prejudice against all monopolies and companies that do any vendor lock-in or try to use proprietary standards instead of open standards or do anything that looks like market capture.  I don't like Facebook, Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, Intel, Valve, Nintendo, Sony, Adobe, Autodesk, and so on and so forth.  They are all using AI or will be soon in almost all aspects of what they do, but that isn't the problem; the problem is that they do things that are anti-consumer and anti-market.  AI isn't inherently anti-consumer or anti-market.

comments.author: Coldfriction
comments.body:
NO.  Indie devs shouldn't have an easy pass just because they are indie.  Sloppily made games don't need an audience one way or the other.  Game jams where people put very little time are the place for idea testing, not Steam and not Next Fest where games shown will be on Steam.

If you allow ALL art into your gallery without any curation, and accept crayon stick figures with everything else and do almost no curation, how many people will look at the good art vs just turn away and avoid your gallery?

Steam isn't a place for indies to gain traction anymore.  If you don't end up promoted by Valve or others and shown at the "front" of the "store" you lose and the game was pointless because there is no curation.  You're hoping Valve "sponsors" you or enough other random people "vote" for you to get attention.  The random people voting are looking at a "ballot" of thousands of options.

AI devs need to go to direct sales to the customers.  They need to operate outside of Valve.  Minecraft did and it still requires no launcher.  Not a fan that it requires an account at all for single player still though.  I have SIX paid for Minecraft accounts in my house and still there are people that come over that want to play a quick game on my LAN (I have like 10 computers in my house) and can't set up their own character to play with everyone else.  I know how to run cracked copies, but still this "account" based gaming hurts LAN parties and friends playing together a LOT.

comments.body: AI has it's place as a tool, like if a dev needs to make a forest AI can make that forest quickly and effectively. However if it's used to replace Devs, creating core mechanics and to rush things through, without proper testing (which was already happening before AI to be fair) it just creates a product that is not good enough. AI isn't even the correct term for these tools they are LLMs and as a society we need to stop treating them as more than just tools. Also there is a lot of sense that games are meant to be art and AI isn't capable of producing the human element art needs for humans to connect to it.
